canonical_statement: The paper evaluates whether a knowledge-graph store for agent-written knowledge can make strict write gating, bitemporal governance, partitioned trust, non-widening composition, and in-store auditability native storage guarantees.

Quipu inverts four conventional defaults: accept-then-clean becomes refusal at the gate, one or no time axis becomes bitemporal data and governance, flat trust becomes partitioned trust with non-widening composition, and external governance becomes in-store governance facts and queries.

GS1 requires every governed fact to pass predicates evaluated against the pending post-state before the write enters the store, while writes that touch no governed target skip policy-claim evaluation.
GS2 persists every allow, deny, or unknown gate outcome as a signed time-indexed verdict outside the judged write transaction so that denial evidence survives rollback.

GS3 attaches authority to graph partitions and intersects authority along delegation chains; an empty intersection refuses the write, relabelling requires meta-partition authority, and overlays bind once to a parent.

GS4 makes composition non-widening by folding freshness and trust with meet, obligations with join, and coverage separately; partial coverage fails enforcement floors and cross-chain trust refuses comparison.
GS5 stores the governance specification, trace, and verdicts together and defines the audit as a deterministic query that distinguishes violations from incompleteness.
GS6 replays governance decisions against the facts, labels, shapes, and policies that were in force at the decision transaction rather than against latest-only rules.

The storage model is an append-only bitemporal EAVT fact log keyed by entity, attribute, value, named graph, transaction, valid interval, and a three-valued operation of assert, retract, or tombstone.

canonical_statement: Named graphs partition authority and trust, overlays preserve a bind-once parent relation, datasets compose graph views, and imported knowledge packs preserve content identity across stores by content hash.

The governed writer stages candidate facts inside a savepoint, intersects writer authority, evaluates policy claims and SHACL constraints over the staged post-state, then either commits or rolls back while recording a signed verdict in either case.

The implementation is a Rust crate backed by one SQLite file, with a custom SPARQL 1.1 evaluator and CLI, REST, and MCP interfaces; the reported implementation contains roughly 67,000 lines of code and more than 1,000 tests.
Storage grew linearly at about 8.3 KB per ingested episode from 1,000 to 20,000 episodes; the authors present this as engineering characterization rather than a comparison with other stores.
An interned-term cache produced a reported 3.9 to 4.9 times constant-factor improvement in the nested-loop basic graph pattern evaluator.
The in-memory read-model prototype reduced the reported two-hop join latency from 133 seconds to 0.15 milliseconds at about 385 bytes of resident memory per fact.

canonical_statement: Census is a deterministic seeded multi-writer lifecycle with a gated arm and the same scripted control arm with gates disabled; no LLM runs in the core benchmark loop, so planted defects and counts are known by construction.

The Census lifecycle uses six phases, three district graphs, three recorder identities, four policies, six planted defects, 100 clean writes, seven composition probes, a mid-run policy amendment, and replay and external-checker export steps.
For the deterministic benchmark manifests, three consecutive repeats for each seed and arm produced byte-identical manifests, and the external-checker export was byte-stable.

canonical_statement: The three-plane container checklist marked 56 of 64 DEMM cases sufficient and had an overclaim rate of 0.750.

Quipu's internal validity checker achieved zero overclaim by rejecting every degraded record, which stopped false sufficiency claims but did not localize which governance properties remained supported.

Quipu was added by the authors as a ninth DEMM regime, and the degradation adapter and content reader were also authored for this study, so the external-benchmark result supports claims about Quipu's record format rather than an independent leaderboard comparison.

canonical_statement: The first DEMM pass exposed an attribution weakness in denial evidence, after which the store was changed to bind actor and principal-chain attribution into the signed verdict evidence hash; the paper reports the post-fix results.
The paper explicitly does not claim comparative query-performance superiority, does not treat trust labels as access control, and does not claim full denial outcome re-derivation after rollback.

The source and benchmark artifacts behind the reported numbers are archived at Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21878429 for release v0.3.20, with concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21878428 and development repository github.com/scbrown/quipu.
The author reports implementation and drafting assistance from Claude by Anthropic.

The authors conclude that strict write gating, bitemporal governance, partitioned trust, non-widening composition, and signed in-store audit evidence can be implemented together and tested deterministically on agent-written knowledge workloads.
The stated next steps are broader controlled agent experiments across tasks and models and a portable governed-store specification that other storage systems could claim and be scored against.
